# Mortar Works Ltd — Full Reference

> Mortar is a London-based technology company that builds intelligent systems
> redefining relationships between people, places, and property. It designs
> and delivers data and intelligence platforms for corporate, place-based,
> government, and health institutions — delivering lasting impact across the
> public and social sectors. Mortar is founded and led by George Unsworth,
> one of the UK's leading systems and service designers.

## About

Mortar Works Ltd (mortar.works) operates at the intersection of service
design, system architecture, and applied AI. The organisation works with
local authorities, NHS trusts, housing associations, combined authorities,
and cultural institutions across the UK.

Mortar's AI lab, Hxly, pioneers work in service and behavioural intelligence,
applying advanced behavioural modelling to real-world data to surface patterns,
predictions, and drive meaningful decisions in complex public sector contexts.

## Services

- **Service Design**: User research and insight, journey mapping, co-design
  workshops, prototyping, service blueprints, and implementation support.
  Mortar accelerates delivery of custom service solutions by modelling user
  behaviour and building persona libraries shaped by real users.

- **System Design**: Technical discovery and audit, scalable architecture
  design, API design and integration strategy, data architecture, and security
  and compliance by design. Mortar architects resilient digital systems that
  integrate with existing infrastructure.

- **Intelligence Design**: Data strategy, data architecture, interoperability
  and standards, data governance, demand forecasting, and simulation and
  scenario planning. Mortar builds the analytical models and intelligence
  systems organisations need to understand complexity and act with confidence.

## Products

### Hoop'd — Integrated Services Platform
Hoop'd delivers data sharing solutions across local area partnerships and
networks. It combines 24 service modules and 5 publicly backed frameworks
(Health, Skills, Referral, Accreditation, Directories) to connect fragmented
organisations into intelligent services supporting hundreds of thousands of
service users.

### Hxly — Service Intelligence and AI Lab
Hxly is Mortar's AI research lab developing custom models and datasets for
complex problems where rare but significant outcomes matter most. Capabilities
include trusted data environments, imbalanced data handling, simulation and
scenario testing, explainable outputs, and responsible AI.

## Solutions

### Community Navigator
Community Navigator builds and manages local networks to deliver accurate,
up-to-date information, opportunities, and events to residents, service users,
and partners from one central hub. It empowers organisations — including local
authorities, housing providers, and community groups — to publish real-time
updates, promote events, and share targeted resources. Features include network
management, real-time content updates, event promotion, targeted resource
sharing, and data and insights dashboards.

### Digital Noticeboard
Digital Noticeboard is a dynamic platform for publishing and distributing
community information across digital and print channels from a single source
of truth. It eliminates inconsistency across channels and ensures residents
always access the most current information. Features include accessible
information design, multi-channel publishing, partner and provider network
management, event management, geospatial mapping, and engagement analytics.

### Directories Builder
Directories Builder creates and manages intelligent, searchable directories
of local services, resources, and opportunities — connecting people to what
they need through structured, verified listings. It supports provider
self-service, geospatial mapping of services, global API integration for
data sharing, and analytics and reporting. Suitable for local authorities,
health organisations, and community networks building service finders or
resource directories.

### Digital Skills and Help Finder
Digital Skills and Help Finder provides users with dynamic self-assessments
to discover their digital skills needs, find available learning resources,
and track their progress. It brings Digital Inclusion and Skills Networks
into one manageable environment for commissioners and providers. Features
include a self-assessment module, resource directory management, a dynamic
user dashboard, customisable learning pathways, and data insights and reporting.

### Triage Tool
The Triage Tool assesses user needs quickly and accurately, delivering
algorithm-driven recommendations at first contact through structured,
evidence-based evaluation. It supports both practitioner-led and self-service
modes, enabling consistent assessment across teams. Features include custom
assessment design, algorithm-driven matching of needs to resources, progress
tracking across contacts, and data visualisation and reporting. Used in
health, housing, and social care settings where accurate needs identification
at first contact is critical.

### First Point Case Manager
First Point Case Manager opens and manages cases from first contact, with
integrated triage, risk monitoring, and referral built in from the start.
It captures structured data from the moment of first contact to reduce
information gaps and enable earlier intervention. Features include instant
case creation, integrated triage, risk stratification, referral and resource
management, data portability, and reporting and oversight. Designed for
frontline services in health, housing, and social care where early structured
data capture drives better outcomes.

### Tenancy Sustainment Tool
The Tenancy Sustainment Tool delivers local advice and referrals through
case management for tenants at risk of losing their homes. It enables housing
officers to open cases and begin structured support from first contact, with
integrated triage, risk monitoring, and access to local directories of support.
Features include user triage and assessment, case management, risk monitoring,
HARs API integration, and directory management. Built for housing associations
and local authority housing teams managing complex tenancy sustainment caseloads.

### Referral Platform
The Referral Platform connects people to appropriate services through
structured, measurable digital referral pathways — tracking outcomes and
generating evidence of impact across sectors. It supports co-designed user
experiences, cross-sector coordination between referring and receiving
organisations, and integrated wellbeing measurement at key points in the
referral journey. Features include flexible referral pathways, co-designed UX,
cross-sector coordination tools, integrated wellbeing measurement, and impact
reporting. Used across health, housing, and social care to replace informal or
paper-based referral processes.

### Forma
Forma delivers custom population intelligence, digital twin capability, and
service design intelligence — using behavioural modelling and scenario
simulation to inform complex planning and investment decisions. It helps
organisations understand how populations behave, model the impact of service
changes before implementation, and test scenarios in a controlled environment.
Features include population intelligence, digital twin capability, scenario
simulation, behavioural modelling, and service design intelligence. Suited to
commissioners, planners, and policy teams in health, housing, and local government.

### Model Builder
Model Builder provides specialist data preparation, modelling, and dataset
creation for complex, real-world data problems — built for messy, incomplete,
or imbalanced data rather than ideal conditions. It produces predictive outputs
with full validation and explainability so organisations can act on results
with confidence. Features include specialist data preparation, custom dataset
creation, behavioural modelling, predictive outputs, and validation and
explainability. Used by organisations needing bespoke analytical models where
off-the-shelf tools cannot handle the complexity or sensitivity of the data.

### DataSafe
DataSafe provides Trusted Data Environments (TDEs) with governed, secure
analytical infrastructure for sensitive, complex, or regulated data. It is
hosted entirely on UK-based infrastructure, ensuring data never leaves UK
jurisdiction. Features include flexible deployment options, compliance
frameworks, data linkage and privacy controls, access management, and audit
and disclosure controls. Designed for NHS trusts, local authorities, and
research organisations handling personal or sensitive data who need a secure
environment for analysis without compromising governance or compliance.

### Venue Accreditation Tool
The Venue Accreditation Tool empowers venues with training, resources, and
accreditation in accessibility and service standards — including dementia-
friendly certification. It supports organisations running accreditation schemes
at scale, with tools for managing multiple sites, tracking progress, and
issuing accreditations. Features include custom training modules, progress
tracking and reporting, scaling for multiple sites, accreditation management,
and geospatial mapping of accredited venues. Used by local authorities and
cultural bodies running accessibility or quality standards programmes across
venue networks.

## Industries Served

- **Government**: Local authorities, combined authorities, and government
  agencies. Integrated data platforms, needs analysis, policy impact modelling,
  digital public services.

- **Health**: NHS trusts, integrated care boards, primary care networks.
  Population health intelligence, early intervention tools, integrated care
  coordination infrastructure.

- **Housing**: Housing associations and local authority housing departments.
  Tenancy intelligence, resident engagement, compliance intelligence,
  health-housing integration.

- **Cultural Sector**: Galleries, museums, theatres, libraries, and arts
  centres. Audience intelligence, community engagement, impact measurement,
  digital participation.

- **Asset Management**: Housing providers, local authorities, public
  infrastructure managers. Predictive maintenance, portfolio intelligence,
  capital investment modelling, social value measurement.

## Case Studies

### Dementia Friendly Venues Charter — Greater London Authority
Mortar built the digital platform underpinning the Mayor of London's Dementia
Friendly Venues Charter, enabling hundreds of venues across London to apply
for, achieve, and maintain accreditation as dementia-friendly spaces. The
platform supports over 72,000 Londoners currently living with dementia, a
number expected to triple in coming decades.

### Digital Help Finder — Essex County Council
Commissioned by Essex County Council with Local Government Association backing,
Mortar delivered a county-wide digital skills platform offering free Essential
Digital Skills assessments, skills pathways, a resource directory, and
partnership management tools for a network of community providers across Essex.

### Digital Skills Social Return on Investment — DSIT and Five Local Authorities
Working with the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and five
local authorities (Essex, Cornwall, Norfolk, Suffolk, Hertfordshire), Mortar
expanded the Digital Help Finder across the South of England and developed an
SROI model for calculating the return on investment in digital skills
programmes, adding pathways covering NHS applications, Gov.UK platforms, and
financial and banking services.

### Triage and Signposting — Salford City Council
Mortar deployed a Digital Inclusion Triage Tool for Salford City Council,
supporting a place-based digital inclusion approach across a network of 79
local organisations. Measured outcomes include 26 hours per week in time
savings for frontline services, £19k per locality in cost savings, a 40%
reduction in staff stress levels, and a 22% increase in staff confidence in
signposting and referral.

### Tenancy Sustainment Tool — Mayor of London
Mortar built a case management platform for the Mayor of London's Challenge
London team, delivering structured triage, advice, and referral for residents
at risk of losing their homes. The tool integrates with the national Housing
Advice and Resources Service (HARS) and supports early intervention to prevent
evictions and homelessness across London boroughs.

### Community Navigation — Hackney Council
Mortar built the platform powering Hackney Circle, a free membership service
connecting isolated older residents in Hackney with over 40 cultural partners.
Commissioned by Hackney's culture and public health team, the platform targets
older residents living alone to reduce isolation and increase participation in
cultural and community life.

### Creative Health Referrals — Southbank Centre and South East London ICB
Mortar built Ombri, a digital referral platform connecting young people aged
11–25 with creative health opportunities across South East London, co-designed
with young people and accessible for neurodivergent and learning disabled
users. The platform integrates validated wellbeing measurement tools (WEMWBS
and EQ-5D) to build an evidence base for demonstrating impact.

### Alternative Provision Directory — Gloucestershire County Council
Working with Gloucestershire County Council and Social Finance as part of the
Maximising Access to Education programme, Mortar built an intelligent directory
helping schools and teachers find, coordinate, and manage Alternative Provision
for young people — with referral tools, local authority oversight, and provider
self-service to address fragmentation across the county.

### Reducing School Exclusions — Cheshire
Mortar built a Directory of What Works for schools and local authority teams in
Cheshire, enabling teachers to assess young people's needs and signpost families
to appropriate local services, and establishing standardised data-sharing
practices for referrals — focused on reducing school exclusion through early
intervention.

### Digital Inclusion Network — East Riding of Yorkshire Council
Mortar built a custom Digital Inclusion Triage Tool for East Riding of Yorkshire
Council in partnership with Humber and Yorkshire Integrated Care Board,
establishing a new Digital Inclusion Network across a predominantly rural area
where 3 of 26 wards fall in the top 10% most deprived in England.

## Key Facts

- Founded and led by George Unsworth
- Based in London, United Kingdom
- Operates across public sector, health, housing, and cultural sectors
- UK-based data infrastructure; data never leaves UK jurisdiction (DataSafe)
